key_concepts: A balanced chemical equation has equal numbers of each type of atom on both sides
Coefficients are written before chemical formulas to balance equations
Atoms of each element are counted on the reactant and product sides
Mercury(II) oxide decomposes into mercury and oxygen gas
Aluminum reacts with oxygen to form aluminum oxide
Carbon disulfide reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide
Aluminum reacts with hydrochloric acid to produce aluminum chloride and hydrogen gas
Aluminum bromide reacts with chlorine to produce aluminum chloride and bromine
